text:
sophia: Heads-up: bringing up Atlas customer finetune merge (two LoRA patches: conv2 + inst-tune). Seeing tokenizer token-id shifts after merge; quick smoke failing on entity normalization and numeric formatting.

raj: which smoke tests are failing? paste 1-2 failing examples.

sophia: Example 1:
```
PROMPT: "Summarize the meeting on 2024-11-03 regarding the Q4 pipeline."
EXPECTED: "Meeting on 2024-11-03: ..."
MODEL_OUT (merged-atlas:v2-int4): "Meeting on 2024-11-03\u200d\u200b: ..."  <-- zero-width char inserted, breaks parsing in downstream extractor
```

min: that zero-width looks like a tokenizer merge artifact. Can you run the atlas_quick_eval pack with int4 quant and token-debug on?

sophia: running now:
```
./run_eval --pack atlas_quick_eval --model merged-atlas:v2 --quant int4 --batch 16 --token-debug
```

(eval-bot): Quick eval started: pack=atlas_quick_eval, model=merged-atlas:v2,int4, job=ev-4821

(eval-bot): Quick eval finished: pass_rate=84%, threshold=90%, regressions=6
Top regressions: entity_normalization(3), long_number_format(2), special_token_insertion(1)

carla: Did the merge preserve the finetune tokenizer.json? We usually require using the customer tokenizer for token-id canonicalization. Looks like merge used base/tokenizer v1.2 while finetune had v1.3.

raj: Confirmed — merge script used base tokenizer by mistake. That would shift some token ids and inject hidden chars. Need to remap Lora weights to target tokenizer ids.

min: Use tokenizer remap tool:
```
python tools/tokenizer_remap.py \
  --src-tokenizer artifacts/atlas_fin-tokenizer-v1.3/tokenizer.json \
  --dst-tokenizer artifacts/base-tokenizer-v1.2/tokenizer.json \
  --lora-file artifacts/atlas_lora_patch.pt \
  --out remapped/atlas_lora_patch_remapped.pt
```

min: Also add --preserve-specials to keep customer special token mappings.

sophia: remap finished, remerged, reran quick-eval:
(eval-bot): Quick eval started: pack=atlas_quick_eval, model=merged-atlas:v2-remap,int4, job=ev-4822

(eval-bot): Quick eval finished: pass_rate=93%, threshold=90%, regressions=1, latency_avg_ms=76, latency_prev_ms=72
Notes: entity_normalization fixed, remaining regression is a minor punctuation spacing issue around em-dash. Latency +4ms avg (likely small cache alignment due to remapped token ids).

carla: Good fix. Let's add a unit test that checks token-id mapping for these 5 customer-specific tokens and block merges when mismatch >0.

raj: PR opened with tokenizer check + tests + repro examples: https://git.company/repo/pull/827 (includes failing snippet and remap integration).

min: small follow-up: saw a rare stacktrace in logs during canary: "kv_cache_length_mismatch at serve/kvcache.go:142" when long prompt with preserved specials triggered. Workaround: enforce max_prefix_len=2048 for merged model in canary rollout.

carla: rollout plan: canary 5% traffic 2h -> 25% 6h -> 100% with automatic rollback on pass_rate < 90% or error_rate spike > 0.5%. Use this rollout snippet in console:
```
{
  "model": "merged-atlas:v2-remap",
  "canary": [{"pct":5, "duration":"2h"}, {"pct":25, "duration":"6h"}],
  "fallback": "atlas-base:v3",
  "checks": {"quick_eval_pack":"atlas_quick_eval", "min_pass":90}
}
```

sophia: thanks. I'll notify Atlas support and enable eval-alerting for 48h. Also tagging @ops to watch latency dashboards. :eyes: :+1:

raj: leaving notes in the customer runbook about tokenizer version pinning for future merges.

sophia: closing loop — major cause was tokenizer id mismatch during LoRA merge; remap + extra tests fixed it. Will monitor canary.

carla: nice catch.
